title: Golden Oat Porridge
description: Creamy oats simmered with turmeric, cinnamon and a spoonful of maple for a warm start to the day.
steps: Tip the oats, milk, turmeric and cinnamon into a small pan and set over a medium heat.
Stir often for 8 to 10 minutes until the oats are soft and the porridge falls slowly from the spoon.
Sweeten with the maple syrup and taste, adding a splash more milk if you prefer it looser.
Spoon into bowls and finish with the toasted almonds.

title: Herb Garden Omelette
description: A soft three-egg omelette folded around parsley, chives and a little melting cheese.
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and plenty of pepper until the yolks and whites are one colour.
Melt the butter in a small non-stick pan over a medium heat until it foams.
Pour in the eggs and draw the setting edges into the centre for about two minutes.
Scatter over the herbs and cheese, fold the omelette in half and slide it onto a warm plate.

title: Sunrise Berry Smoothie Bowl
description: Frozen berries and banana blitzed thick enough to eat with a spoon, then piled with seeds.
steps: Put the frozen berries, banana, oat milk and almond butter into a blender.
Blend in short bursts, scraping down the sides, until the mixture is thick and scoopable rather than pourable.
Divide between two bowls and smooth the tops with the back of a spoon.
Finish with the pumpkin seeds and coconut and eat straight away while still frozen.

title: Lemon Chickpea Salad
description: Chickpeas tossed with cucumber, red onion and a bright lemon and olive oil dressing.
steps: Whisk the lemon juice, olive oil, a good pinch of salt and plenty of pepper in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas and turn them through the dressing so they soak it up while you chop.
Fold in the cucumber, red onion and parsley.
Leave to sit for five minutes, then taste and add more lemon or salt before serving.

title: Tomato and Basil Toastie
description: A crisp buttered toastie with sweet tomatoes, torn basil and stretchy mozzarella.
steps: Butter the outside face of each slice of bread so it will crisp in the pan.
Layer the tomato, mozzarella and basil onto the unbuttered side of one slice and season well.
Close the sandwich and cook in a dry pan over a medium heat for three minutes until golden.
Press, flip and cook the second side until the cheese has melted, then cut in half and eat hot.

title: Smoked Paprika Chicken Wraps
description: Strips of paprika-rubbed chicken with charred peppers and a cooling yoghurt drizzle.
steps: Toss the chicken with the smoked paprika, olive oil and a good pinch of salt.
Fry over a high heat for six minutes without moving it much so the strips colour deeply.
Add the pepper and cook for a further five minutes until softened and lightly charred.
Stir the lime juice into the yoghurt, warm the tortillas and build the wraps with chicken, pepper and drizzle.

title: Slow-Simmered Lentil Stew
description: A hearty pot of green lentils and root vegetables cooked down until thick and glossy.
steps: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the olive oil over a low heat for ten minutes.
Stir in the garlic and tomato puree and cook for a minute until it smells sweet rather than sharp.
Add the lentils and stock, bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for thirty minutes.
Mash a ladleful against the side of the pan to thicken the stew, then season generously and serve.

title: Weeknight Salmon Traybake
description: Salmon fillets roasted over new potatoes and green beans with lemon and dill.
ingredients: 1 lemon, half sliced and half for juice
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and toss the potatoes with half the olive oil and plenty of salt in a roasting tray.
Roast for fifteen minutes until the cut sides are starting to crisp.
Add the beans, nestle in the salmon, top with lemon slices and the remaining oil.
Return to the oven for ten minutes until the salmon flakes, then finish with dill and lemon juice.

title: Mushroom Barley Risotto
description: Pearl barley stirred slowly with mushrooms and thyme into a nutty, savoury risotto.
steps: Fry the mushrooms in half the butter over a high heat until deeply browned, then set them aside.
Soften the onion in the remaining butter, add the barley and thyme and toast for two minutes.
Add the hot stock a ladleful at a time, stirring, for about thirty minutes until the barley is tender but chewy.
Fold the mushrooms and cheese back in, rest for two minutes off the heat and serve loose rather than stiff.

title: Spiced Butternut Curry
description: Butternut squash simmered in coconut milk with ginger, cumin and a handful of spinach.
steps: Soften the onion in the coconut oil for eight minutes, then stir in the ginger and ground spices.
Add the squash and turn it through the spice paste until every piece is coated.
Pour in the coconut milk, half fill the tin with water and add that too, then simmer for twenty minutes.
Stir the spinach through in handfuls until it wilts, season well and serve with rice.

title: Dark Chocolate Mousse
description: A light set mousse made with dark chocolate and whipped egg whites, chilled until airy.
steps: Melt the chocolate and butter together in a bowl set over barely simmering water, then cool for five minutes.
Beat the egg yolks into the warm chocolate one at a time until the mixture is thick and shiny.
Whisk the whites with the salt to soft peaks, add the sugar and whisk to a firm glossy meringue.
Fold the meringue into the chocolate in three additions, keeping the air in, then chill for four hours.

title: Honey Roast Plums
description: Halved plums roasted with honey and vanilla until they collapse into their own syrup.
steps: Heat the oven to 190C and sit the plums cut side up in a snug baking dish.
Spoon over the honey and vanilla and tuck the orange peel between the fruit.
Roast for twenty minutes, basting once, until the plums are soft and sitting in a dark syrup.
Serve warm with the yoghurt and the syrup spooned from the dish.

title: No-Bake Peanut Oat Bars
description: Chewy oat and peanut butter bars pressed into a tin and set in the fridge, no oven needed.
steps: Warm the peanut butter and maple syrup together and stir until they pour smoothly from the spoon.
Mix in the oats and salt until every oat is coated, then let the mixture cool for five minutes.
Stir through the chocolate chips and press the mixture very firmly into a lined tin.
Chill for at least two hours before cutting into eight bars.
